target_customer: Customer service and sales teams at mid-size and large companies (at the time of the YC batch, enterprises needing typo-free, on-brand writing; today, support teams buying AI agents)
problem: Support and sales agents lose time and quality to typos and slow writing; later, companies want customer requests resolved end to end without human effort.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (text prediction for customer service teams in 2022; AI agent platform for customer service now)
product_category: Customer service AI, originally privacy-first text prediction and keyboard

founders.name: David Eberle
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as former Engagement Manager at Booz & Company; education not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Janis Berneker
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Lead Data Science at SRF; education not found in opened sources.

competitors.name: Google Gboard and built-in phone keyboards
competitors.what: Default keyboards with next-word prediction and autocorrect
competitors.traction_then: Ubiquitous on Android and iOS; Typewise's own claim is that it outperforms Google and Apple

competitors.name: Gboard (consumer keyboard comparison)
competitors.what: Android Police compared Typewise to Gboard on accuracy and privacy

technical_complexity.rationale: Offline on-device prediction and typo correction with a custom hexagonal layout needed real NLP work for a two-person team, but it was not research-grade; the later agent platform builds on commodity LLMs.

defensibility.rationale: Text prediction was a feature that Google, Apple and Microsoft could ship for free; the later moat is integrations with helpdesks and enterprise deployments, which is moderate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large platforms kept shipping free prediction, which pushed Typewise to leave the consumer keyboard in 2022. No acquisition was found as of the search.

market_need_then: The consumer keyboard had 2 million downloads (company claim) but weak monetisation; enterprise support teams were a clearer paying market, and the YC launch post claims 20 percent writing efficiency gains for Fortune 500 pilots.

branding.name_origin: From the idea of typing wisely and a wise way of typing, according to a founder interview. The product was first called WRIO Keyboard.
branding.domain_note: Company now uses typewise.app; earlier domain history not found.

identity.visual_style: Distinct hexagonal key layout in the consumer app

rebrands.why: Founder interview says Typewise better reflected the vision of wise typing

branding.community_and_virality: Android Police and Product Hunt coverage of the keyboard; 2 million downloads claimed.

brand_strength.rationale: Consumer app earned press and 2 million downloads, but the brand is little known in the enterprise AI space.

pivots.to: B2B text prediction for customer service, later end-to-end AI customer service agents and the Nova operator
pivots.why: Typewise says it moved to business software around YC S22; later AI wave shifted the product to agents.

outcome_analysis: Typewise started as a Kickstarter-backed consumer keyboard and raised small angel, grant and crowdfunding rounds before YC S22. It pivoted into B2B customer service software and now lists enterprise logos such as Galaxus, DPD and Superhuman. Funding disclosed since YC is thin and mostly from aggregators, so growth looks capital light but the true raise is unknown.
notes: Funding totals conflict across aggregators (CB Insights 7.69M over 11 rounds including an Aug 2025 Mitel accelerator entry; ZoomInfo 2.9M; FundedIQ 2.4M). These are unverified and excluded. Kickstarter raised about 17000 dollars (Wikipedia says 2015) and is excluded as pre-company. Wikipedia dates the crowdfunding to CHF 1.8M (about 1.7M euro); Typewise blog says 1.7M euro (2M dollars); EU-Startups also reported it (403 on fetch). The 500K YC amount comes from Wikipedia. Founding year conflicts: 2019 per Wikipedia and company site, 2020 per YC page. B2B customer service AI rivals around 2022 were not sourced, so only keyboard incumbents are listed. EU-Startups fetch was blocked and not worked around.
